misconceptions.believed: An idle redraw tick can safely resolve a held Escape: it is only ambiguous until more bytes arrive, and if none did, it was a bare Escape.
misconceptions.revealed_by: Driving the real editor through a pty. Shift-Tab had put the literal characters '[Z' into the buffer twice, and the run failed with SyntaxError. The redraw loop calls flush() every 50ms, so any escape sequence whose bytes straddle a tick was torn into an Escape key followed by its remaining bytes as text.
misconceptions.corrected_to: Held input resolves only after ESCAPE_TIMEOUT of genuine silence, measured from the last byte received. Below that, flush() returns nothing and keeps waiting.
misconceptions.generalisable_lesson: Every headless test passed, because feed(ESC) followed by feed('[A') is adjacent in a test and separated by time in reality. A component can be correct through its own interface and wrong in the loop that drives it; the bug lived entirely in the timing between two calls, which is a property only a real terminal has.

misconceptions.believed: tokenize is fast and buffers are small, so re-highlighting the whole buffer on every keystroke fits the frame budget.
misconceptions.revealed_by: A latency test written to record a number rather than to catch anything. It failed at 26.2ms against a 16ms budget on a 400-line buffer: tokenising 400 lines to draw 18 of them.
misconceptions.corrected_to: highlight_window tokenises only the visible slice, dedenting it so tokenize accepts an indented start and shifting the resulting columns back. Worst case fell to 12.69ms on a buffer ten times larger.
misconceptions.generalisable_lesson: The exit criterion said 'measured, not asserted'. Writing the measurement as a test turned an assumption into a number; an assertion of the form 'this is fast enough' would have passed forever.

decisions.decision: Editing logic is a separate module from drawing
alternatives: One editor class owning both buffer and screen
decisions.rationale: Makes correctness provable headless, and means a renderer bug can never be a text bug.

decisions.decision: A dependency-free cell grid with a frame diff
decisions.rationale: 30 cells per keystroke instead of 1920, and curses is a dependency N1 forbids.

decisions.decision: Restoration by three mechanisms, with an idempotent restore()
decisions.rationale: Each mechanism misses a case the others catch, and overlapping them costs nothing.

decisions.decision: A held Escape resolves on a timeout, not on an idle tick
alternatives: Resolve whenever a read returns nothing
decisions.rationale: M7: the eager version tears escape sequences apart and types them into the buffer.

decisions.decision: Only the visible window is tokenised
decisions.rationale: M8: cost must scale with the window, not the file.

alternatives: Feed cadence into the elegance axis
decisions.rationale: N5: what an even cadence means about a programmer is not established, so it must not be scored.

decisions.decision: Reverse video is emitted at Depth.NONE; colour is not
alternatives: Suppress every attribute, as Renderer.paint does
decisions.rationale: The block cursor is drawn with reverse video, so suppressing it leaves NO_COLOR users with no visible cursor. Reverse video is not colour.

decisions.decision: The editor banks a cleared level in full rather than as practice
alternatives: Treat it as practice, as cmd_play does for a file on disk
decisions.rationale: This front-end knows the real solve time, so the Speed axis is honest. It is the case cmd_play's own comment anticipated.

friction.description: The captured pty transcript showed no restore sequences, which looked like a serious bug for twenty minutes. The harness was closing the pty before the child's final write; the application had been restoring correctly all along.

Two early editor tests failed on the assertion rather than the code: one matched \033[3 and caught cursor positioning rather than colour, the other asserted a scroll offset before the frame that computes it had been composed.
Whether the motion is pleasant over a long session cannot be established without a person at a terminal. Same gap S002 recorded for the presentation layer.

open_questions.question: The pty suite tests restoration but not decoding. M7 was a timing bug that every headless test passed. Should the pty harness grow a 'deliver these bytes with these delays' mode, and would that have caught it?
Rhythm data is collected and shown but never stored. Is it worth persisting locally so the profiler can use process signal as well as residue, and what is the consent story if so?
Two modules now turn an RGB into an escape code: Renderer.paint for strings and Editor.style for cells. Should the grid consume Renderer output, or Renderer emit style prefixes?
W8 wants the axes to assemble as tests report, which needs _harness.py to stream per-test results rather than return one object. Worth a protocol change, or is the animated reveal enough?
There is no way to save the buffer, so a crash mid-level loses the work. Is a scratch file the answer, or does that reintroduce the disk round-trip the editor exists to remove?
